Training Latent Diffusion Models with Interacting Particle Algorithms

The paper’s statements first; additional assumptions and new theorems second. Mathematics and exact Lean code appear side by side.

Source: Wang, Kuntz and Akyildiz, local manuscript. Main text with line numbers · Supplement with line numbers · Source audit and coverage · Exact source inventory

Paper assumptionsPaper resultsCorrectionsNew assumptionsNew theoremsMain numerical boundCheck the statements

Formalization status. All 19 source result statements are stated below, including appendix restatements. The normalized variational identity and marginal optimizer are proved on explicit domains. Continuous-time rates require entropy and transport premises; the full Wasserstein and SDE arguments remain incomplete. A displayed source statement is not a claim of a completed Lean proof. Each card identifies the checked endpoint and any remaining gap.

Blue identifies extra premises needed by a formal endpoint; rose identifies corrections. Orange is reserved for the new theory in Part II. Lean signatures are extracted from the current source; declaration links open complete proofs. “New” means added relative to this manuscript. Lean uses m or rho for λ; N in the cloud modules counts the paper’s total M × N.

Part I — Results from the paper

Paper assumptions — A1–A4

Write a=(θ,ϕ)a=(\theta,\phi)a=(θ,ϕ), Um(a,z)=−log⁡p~a(xm,z)U_m(a,z)=-\log\tilde p_a(x^m,z)Um​(a,z)=−logp~​a​(xm,z), Zm(a)=∫e−Um(a,z) dzZ_m(a)=\int e^{-U_m(a,z)}\,dzZm​(a)=∫e−Um​(a,z)dz, and πam=Zm(a)−1e−Um(a,⋅)dz\pi_a^m=Z_m(a)^{-1}e^{-U_m(a,\cdot)}dzπam​=Zm​(a)−1e−Um​(a,⋅)dz. The evidence and energy are

ℓ(a)=1M∑mlog⁡Zm(a),F(a,q)=−ℓ(a)+1M∑mKL(qm∥πam).\ell(a)=\frac1M\sum_m\log Z_m(a),\qquad F(a,q)=-\ell(a)+\frac1M\sum_m\mathrm{KL}(q^m\|\pi_a^m).ℓ(a)=M1​m∑​logZm​(a),F(a,q)=−ℓ(a)+M1​m∑​KL(qm∥πam​).

Here ℓ\ellℓ and FFF abbreviate the paper's tilted evidence ℓ~\widetilde\ellℓ and energy F~\widetilde FF. The source cards below retain tildes. In the model-bias theorem in Part II, ℓ\ellℓ explicitly denotes the original, untilted evidence.

The paper uses the normalized product distance d((a,q),(b,r))2=∥a−b∥2+M−1∑mW2(qm,rm)2d((a,q),(b,r))^2=\|a-b\|^2+M^{-1}\sum_m W_2(q^m,r^m)^2d((a,q),(b,r))2=∥a−b∥2+M−1∑m​W2​(qm,rm)2, with M>0M>0M>0. The law qmq^mqm is the latent posterior approximation for datum mmm; NNN is the particle count per datum. The optimizer targets tilted evidence, not automatically the original likelihood.

A1 — Model regularity

Mathematical statement

Put a=(θ,ϕ)a=(\theta,\phi)a=(θ,ϕ), ρ~a(z)=p~a(x,z)\tilde\rho_a(z)=\tilde p_a(x,z)ρ~​a​(z)=p~​a​(x,z), and π~a(z)=ρ~a(z)/Aa\tilde\pi_a(z)=\tilde\rho_a(z)/A_aπ~a​(z)=ρ~​a​(z)/Aa​. For every zzz, the maps a↦π~a(z)a\mapsto\tilde\pi_a(z)a↦π~a​(z) and a↦Aaa\mapsto A_aa↦Aa​ are differentiable. For every aaa, the spatial map z↦π~a(z)z\mapsto\tilde\pi_a(z)z↦π~a​(z) is C2C^2C2, and ρ~a(z)>0\tilde\rho_a(z)>0ρ~​a​(z)>0 everywhere.

import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Defs
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Basic

import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic

/-!
# Literal source regularity contracts

These are assumption translations, not existence theorems. In particular the
paper's universal solution premise includes strictly positive classical densities
at time zero even for arbitrary finite-second-moment initial laws. It is recorded
literally so that this strength is visible; it is not inferred from the other
source assumptions or used to hide an analytic bridge.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace LatentDiffusion.SourceAssumptions

open MeasureTheory Set
open scoped NNReal

variable {P Z : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup P] [NormedSpace ℝ P]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Z] [NormedSpace ℝ Z]

/-- The source's normalized tilted posterior, with the normalizing constant
provided as model data. Normalization and existence of this constant are part of
the model interpretation, not proved by the regularity contract. -/

/-- The manuscript's model-regularity assumption. Parameter differentiability is
pointwise in the latent state; spatial regularity is pointwise in the parameter. -/

/-- The time-space domain in the source's C^{1,2} density assumption. -/

/-- Explicit partial derivatives and their joint continuity on the closed positive
time half-space. Time derivatives at zero are right derivatives, not derivatives
of an extension to negative time. This is the C^{1,2} meaning used here. -/

variable [MeasurableSpace Z]

/-- All data in a source classical solution. `flowEquation` is the actual gradient
flow equation chosen by the application, rather than a scalar energy estimate.
The density is required to realize the initial law as well as later laws. -/

/-- Literal universal solution-regularity premise: every parameter and every
finite-second-moment initial probability law admits the classical solution above.
This includes the source's density regularity and positivity at t=0. -/

section Potential

variable {H I : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H]

/-- The source's joint strong-log-concavity premise, expressed for each negative
log tilted density `U i` in the full parameter-latent pair space. -/

/-- The source's differentiable joint log-likelihood and positive global
gradient-Lipschitz constant. Negating a log density preserves this bound. -/

end Potential

end LatentDiffusion.SourceAssumptions

\begin{restatable}[Model regularity]{assumption_app}{modelregularityrestatable}\label{assump:model_reg}
    We assume that
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item For all $z \in \sZ$, $(\theta,\phi) \mapsto \tilde\pi_{\theta,\phi}(z)$ and $(\theta, \phi) \mapsto A_{\theta, \phi}$ are differentiable;
        \item for all $(\theta,\phi) \in \Theta \times \Phi$, $\tilde\pi_{\theta,\phi}$ is twice continuously differentiable;
        \item $\tilde{\rho}_{\theta,\phi}(z)>0$ for all $z\in \sZ$ and $(\theta,\phi) \in \Theta \times \Phi$.
    \end{enumerate}
\end{restatable}

A2 — Classical solutions for every initial law

assump:solution_reg · main_aistats.tex:151–154

Mathematical statement

For every parameter a0a_0a0​ and every collection μ01:M∈P2(Z)M\mu_0^{1:M}\in\mathcal P_2(Z)^Mμ01:M​∈P2​(Z)M, the source assumes a classical solution of its gradient flow with those initial values. The parameter path is C1C^1C1 on [0,∞)[0,\infty)[0,∞). Each law has a positive Lebesgue density qtm(z)q_t^m(z)qtm​(z), jointly C1,2C^{1,2}C1,2 in time and space on [0,∞)×Z[0,\infty)\times Z[0,∞)×Z.

The Lean contract uses a supplied reference measure ν\nuν, instantiated by Lebesgue measure, and the actual flow equation as an explicit predicate. Its C1,2C^{1,2}C1,2 contract requires continuous first time derivatives and first and second spatial derivatives, including right time derivatives at zero.

Source issue. The universal quantifier includes singular initial laws, while the density and positivity conditions include t=0t=0t=0. This premise is displayed literally and is not claimed to follow from A1, A3 or A4. The source audit records the resulting limitation.

Exact statement as printed in the paper
\begin{restatable}[Regularity of solutions]{assumption_app}{solutionregularityrestatable}\label{assump:solution_reg}
    For any initial conditions $(\theta, \phi, q^{1:M})\in \mathcal{M}^{1:M}$,  the gradient flow has a classical solution $(\theta_t, \phi_t,  q_t^{1:M})_{t \geq 0}$ with $(\theta_0, \phi_0, q_0^{1:M}) = (\theta, \phi, q^{1:M})$.  
Furthermore, for all $m\in [M]$ and $t \geq 0$, $q_t^m$ has a Lebesgue density in $\mathcal{C}^{1,2}([0, \infty) \times \sZ, \mathbb{R}^+)$ and $(\theta_t, \phi_t) \in \mathcal{C}^1([0, \infty), \Theta \times \Phi)$.
\end{restatable}
Paper assumption / source result

A3 — Joint strong log-concavity

assump:strong_log_concave · main_aistats.tex:155–157

Mathematical statement

For every datum mmm, the tilted joint density is λ\lambdaλ-strongly log-concave in the full pair (a,z)(a,z)(a,z), with one λ>0\lambda>0λ>0. Equivalently, for Um(a,z)=−log⁡p~a(xm,z)U_m(a,z)=-\log\tilde p_a(x^m,z)Um​(a,z)=−logp~​a​(xm,z),

Um(sx+(1−s)y)≤sUm(x)+(1−s)Um(y)−λ2s(1−s)∥x−y∥2,0≤s≤1.U_m(sx+(1-s)y)\le sU_m(x)+(1-s)U_m(y)-\tfrac\lambda2s(1-s)\|x-y\|^2,\quad 0\le s\le1.Um​(sx+(1−s)y)≤sUm​(x)+(1−s)Um​(y)−2λ​s(1−s)∥x−y∥2,0≤s≤1.

The particle-average geometry used below is normalized in the latent coordinates. The same constant does not hold in an unweighted replicated Euclidean norm without accounting for that normalization.

A4 — Joint Lipschitz gradient

assump:lipschitz_grad · main_aistats.tex:200–207

Mathematical statement

Every UmU_mUm​ is differentiable and, for one L>0L>0L>0,

∥∇Um(a,z)−∇Um(a′,z′)∥≤L∥(a,z)−(a′,z′)∥.\|\nabla U_m(a,z)-\nabla U_m(a',z')\|\le L\|(a,z)-(a',z')\|.∥∇Um​(a,z)−∇Um​(a′,z′)∥≤L∥(a,z)−(a′,z′)∥.

Negating the log tilted density leaves the Lipschitz constant unchanged. The source's discretization theorem additionally assumes Lipschitz gradients of the tilting penalty R\mathcal RR; the numerical results below instead expose the complete force and its approximation error directly.

/-!
# Literal source regularity contracts

These are assumption translations, not existence theorems. In particular the
paper's universal solution premise includes strictly positive classical densities
at time zero even for arbitrary finite-second-moment initial laws. It is recorded
literally so that this strength is visible; it is not inferred from the other
source assumptions or used to hide an analytic bridge.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace LatentDiffusion.SourceAssumptions

open MeasureTheory Set
open scoped NNReal

variable {P Z : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup P] [NormedSpace ℝ P]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Z] [NormedSpace ℝ Z]

/-- The source's normalized tilted posterior, with the normalizing constant
provided as model data. Normalization and existence of this constant are part of
the model interpretation, not proved by the regularity contract. -/

/-- The manuscript's model-regularity assumption. Parameter differentiability is
pointwise in the latent state; spatial regularity is pointwise in the parameter. -/

/-- The time-space domain in the source's C^{1,2} density assumption. -/

/-- Explicit partial derivatives and their joint continuity on the closed positive
time half-space. Time derivatives at zero are right derivatives, not derivatives
of an extension to negative time. This is the C^{1,2} meaning used here. -/

variable [MeasurableSpace Z]

/-- All data in a source classical solution. `flowEquation` is the actual gradient
flow equation chosen by the application, rather than a scalar energy estimate.
The density is required to realize the initial law as well as later laws. -/

/-- Literal universal solution-regularity premise: every parameter and every
finite-second-moment initial probability law admits the classical solution above.
This includes the source's density regularity and positivity at t=0. -/

section Potential

variable {H I : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H]

/-- The source's joint strong-log-concavity premise, expressed for each negative
log tilted density `U i` in the full parameter-latent pair space. -/

/-- The source's differentiable joint log-likelihood and positive global
gradient-Lipschitz constant. Negating a log density preserves this bound. -/

end Potential

end LatentDiffusion.SourceAssumptions

104structure LipschitzGradient (U : I → H → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0) : Prop where105  positive : 0 < L106  differentiable : ∀ i, Differentiable ℝ (U i)107  lipschitz : ∀ i, LipschitzWith L (gradient (U i))
Exact statement as printed in the paper
\begin{restatable}[Lipschitz gradient]{assumption_app}{lipschitzgradientrestatable}\label{assump:lipschitz_grad}
The log-likelihood $\tilde\ell^m(\theta, \phi,z_0):=\log \tilde{p}_{\theta,\phi}(x^m,z_0)$ is differentiable and its gradient 
is $L$-Lipschitz for some $L > 0$, \emph{i.e.} for all $(\theta, \phi, z_0), (\theta',\phi', z_0') \in \Theta \times \Phi \times \sZ$,
\begin{align*}
    &\|\nabla \tilde\ell^m(\theta, \phi, z_0) - \nabla \tilde\ell^m(\theta',\phi', z_0')\| \\
    &\qquad \quad \, \leq L\|(\theta, \phi, z_0) - (\theta', \phi', z_0')\|.
\end{align*}
\end{restatable}

Additional domain and analytic premises for the formal endpoints

V1 specifies the normalized finite-KL domain. C1 states the unproved analytic bridges used by the conditional flow theorems. These are additions to the paper’s displayed assumptions. The density identity below is a proved bridge on its stated integrability domain.

Proved on the stated domain

Source objective — Tilting adds the expected penalty

eq:ptildedef and tilted objective · main_aistats.tex:88–110 · eq_app:decomposed_obj · supp_aistats.tex:12–33

Mathematical statement

For measurable ρ≥0\rho\ge0ρ≥0 and R≥0R\ge0R≥0, define ρ~=ρe−R\widetilde\rho=\rho e^{-R}ρ​=ρe−R. If ρ\rhoρ is integrable, then ρ~\widetilde\rhoρ​ is integrable and ∫ρ~≤∫ρ\int\widetilde\rho\le\int\rho∫ρ​≤∫ρ. When the tilted normalizer is positive, log⁡∫ρ~≤log⁡∫ρ\log\int\widetilde\rho\le\log\int\rholog∫ρ​≤log∫ρ.

For q≥0q\ge0q≥0, ρ>0\rho>0ρ>0, with both terms on the right integrable, the literal density free energy satisfies

∫qlog⁡qρe−R dν=∫qlog⁡qρ dν+∫qR dν ≥ ∫qlog⁡qρ dν.\int q\log\frac{q}{\rho e^{-R}}\,d\nu=\int q\log\frac q\rho\,d\nu+\int qR\,d\nu\ \ge\ \int q\log\frac q\rho\,d\nu.∫qlogρe−Rq​dν=∫qlogρq​dν+∫qRdν ≥ ∫qlogρq​dν.

set_option linter.style.header false

/-!
# Additional source results, on their explicit mathematical domains

These theorems reconstruct elementary steps used in the supplied manuscript.
They do not construct optimal transport plans, identify a Wasserstein metric
derivative, or justify differentiation or integration by parts on an unbounded
domain. Those continuum application steps remain separate obligations.

`cauchy_minimizing_sequence` corrects Supplement `lem:cauchy`: a Cauchy
sequence must also be a minimizing sequence. A complete ambient metric space
and lower semicontinuity then give an actual minimizer.
-/

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory Set Filter
open scoped Topology

namespace LatentDiffusion.SourceResults

/-- Corrected Supplement `lem:cauchy`: completeness and lower semicontinuity
identify the limit of a Cauchy *minimizing* sequence as a minimizer.
No unrelated Cauchy sequence supplies this conclusion. -/

/-- The scalar derivative used in Supplement `app:lemma_1st_var` includes
the additive constant one. It disappears only on zero-total-mass directions. -/

/-- Constants represent the same first variation on probability tangent
directions. This proves the precise reason the source may omit `+1`. -/

/-- The source's normalized product metric cancels the `1/M` from the
distributional first variation with the inverse metric's `M`.
The positivity of the data count is essential. -/

/-- The first-order scalar consequence of the source's geodesic-convexity
inequality. This step is proved by taking the right derivative; the existence
and calculus of an actual Wasserstein geodesic is not a premise hidden here. -/

/-- The source's Talagrand-type quadratic growth follows directly from strong
geodesic convexity at a minimizer. This proof needs no entropy dissipation.
The application must still establish the displayed convexity inequality for
its actual displacement interpolation and actual metric distance. -/

/-- The actual tilted density in main-text `eq:ptildedef`. -/

/-- The log-density free energy used by the paper, relative to a base measure. -/

/-- Pointwise tilt identity, including zeros of the trial density. -/

/-- Main-text free-energy decomposition after `eq:free-energy`, proved for
the actual base-density integral. Both integrable summands are explicit. -/

/-- Nonnegative KL regularization raises the density free energy. The KL
interpretation of `R` is independent of this integral inequality. -/

/-- Integrability and evidence order follow from a nonnegative integrable
base density and a measurable nonnegative penalty, as used after main-text
`eq:ptildedef`. The tilted integral is not assumed integrable in advance. -/

/-- Taking logs preserves the source's evidence comparison when the tilted
normalizer is positive. Its positivity must be established for the model. -/

/-- Exact finite uniform expectation over the diffusion time index. This is
the arithmetic mean on `Fin K`, so no sampling or asymptotic premise is used. -/

/-- Supplement `app_eq:diffusion_likelihood` and
`app:one_sample_simplified_diffusion`: without inverse-inclusion scaling,
a uniformly selected summand estimates the average, rather than the sum. -/

/-- Corrected unbiased single-time estimator of a *summed* diffusion
objective: multiply the sampled summand by the number of time indices. -/

end LatentDiffusion.SourceResults

158theorem tilted_freeEnergy_decomposition159    {Z : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Z] (ν : Measure Z) (q ρ R : Z → ℝ)160    (hq : ∀ z, 0 ≤ q z) (hρ : ∀ z, 0 < ρ z)161    (hfree : Integrable (fun z ↦ q z * Real.log (q z / ρ z)) ν)162    (hpenalty : Integrable (fun z ↦ q z * R z) ν) :163    Integrable (fun z ↦ q z * Real.log (q z / tiltedDensity ρ R z)) ν ∧164      densityFreeEnergy ν q (tiltedDensity ρ R) =165        densityFreeEnergy ν q ρ + ∫ z, q z * R z ∂ν

Added analytic premise

V1 — Normalized free energy and finite KL domain

Mathematical statement

Let M>0M>0M>0, let ℓ(a)\ell(a)ℓ(a) be the average tilted log evidence, and let πam\pi_a^mπam​ be the actual normalized posterior probability laws. Set

F(a,q)=−ℓ(a)+1M∑m=1MKL(qm∥πam),KL(qm∥πam)<∞.\mathcal F(a,q)=-\ell(a)+\frac1M\sum_{m=1}^M\mathrm{KL}(q^m\|\pi_a^m),\qquad\mathrm{KL}(q^m\|\pi_a^m)<\infty.F(a,q)=−ℓ(a)+M1​m=1∑M​KL(qm∥πam​),KL(qm∥πam​)<∞.

KL here is the actual measure-theoretic divergence. Finite KL is required before conversion to real numbers. The density-normalization result below proves the log-density integral identity under explicit normalization and entropy-integrability conditions. Those conditions are not inferred from pointwise smoothness.

Exact Lean contract

PosteriorFamily · definition and context

Exact shared Lean context
import Mathlib.InformationTheory.KullbackLeibler.Basic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.ProbabilityMeasure
import Mathlib.Tactic

/-! # The normalized variational problem

The free energy is defined by its canonical normalized form, minus log evidence
plus average actual KL divergence. Admissibility retains finite KL before any
`toReal` conversion. Identifying this definition with a density integral needs
the usual log-integrability and normalization identities; those are not inferred
from pointwise smoothness. The theorem is valid for arbitrary measurable latent
spaces and arbitrary parameter sets, so in particular for tilted latent models.
-/
noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory
open scoped BigOperators ENNReal
namespace LatentDiffusion

variable {A Z : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Z] {M : ℕ}

/-- The tilted log evidence and its normalized posterior at each datum. -/

namespace PosteriorFamily
variable (P : PosteriorFamily A Z M)

/-- Excludes infinite entropy from real arithmetic. -/

/-- The normalized free energy, equal to the log-density definition on its
finite integrability domain. -/





/-- Equality in the variational bound identifies every posterior, using
Gibbs' equality theorem for actual finite measures. -/

/-- Proposition 1, including the unique optimal variational distribution.
No existence of a log-evidence maximizer is assumed or concluded. -/

end PosteriorFamily

/-- The valid zero-tilt comparison requires a true optimum attaining zero
gap. Zero gap only at a tilted optimum is insufficient. -/

/-- A zero-penalty tilted maximizer can fail to maximize the true likelihood.
Both likelihoods and gaps here are exact real numbers on a two-point model. -/

end LatentDiffusion
LatentDiffusion/Variational.lean:22PosteriorFamily
22structure PosteriorFamily (A Z : Type*) [MeasurableSpace Z] (M : ℕ) where23  logEvidence : A → ℝ24  posterior : A → Fin M → ProbabilityMeasure Z

Density bridge — The actual log-density integral equals KL minus log evidence

Mathematical statement

Let ρ>0\rho>0ρ>0 be measurable and integrable relative to ν\nuν, with Z=∫ρ dν>0Z=\int\rho\,\mathrm d\nu>0Z=∫ρdν>0. Put π=(ρ/Z)ν\pi=(\rho/Z)\nuπ=(ρ/Z)ν. Let r≥0r\ge0r≥0 be measurable and integrable under π\piπ, with ∫r dπ=1\int r\,\mathrm d\pi=1∫rdπ=1 and rlog⁡r∈L1(π)r\log r\in L^1(\pi)rlogr∈L1(π). Set qν=rρ/Zq_\nu=r\rho/Zqν​=rρ/Z and q=qννq=q_\nu\nuq=qν​ν.

∫qνlog⁡ ⁣(qνρ) dν=∫log⁡ ⁣(qνρ) dq=KL(q∥π)−log⁡Z.\int q_\nu\log\!\left(\frac{q_\nu}{\rho}\right)\,\mathrm d\nu=\int\log\!\left(\frac{q_\nu}{\rho}\right)\,\mathrm dq=\mathrm{KL}(q\|\pi)-\log Z.∫qν​log(ρqν​​)dν=∫log(ρqν​​)dq=KL(q∥π)−logZ.

The theorem constructs both actual probability measures, proves that KL is finite, and proves integrability of the log ratio and this identity. It permits the relative density to vanish, handling the logarithm on the trial law's almost-sure positive support. Normalization and entropy integrability are explicit hypotheses; deriving entropy dissipation along a flow remains a separate analytic obligation.

/-!
# The actual log-density integral and the normalized KL free energy

This file proves the normalization bridge rather than assuming the variational
identity. A nonnegative relative density has finite actual KL whenever its
entropy integrand is integrable. An unnormalized positive base density `ρ` with
positive finite normalizer `Z` gives an actual probability posterior `ρ/Z`.
For a normalized relative density `r`, the trial law has actual base density
`rρ/Z`. Its integral of `log ((rρ/Z)/ρ)` is proved to equal `KL - log Z`.
Zero values of `r` are handled on the trial law's full-measure positive support.
-/

open scoped ENNReal

namespace LatentDiffusion.Density

variable {E : Type*} [MeasurableSpace E]

/-- The actual measure whose density relative to `ν` is the supplied real `r`. -/

/-- Normalization follows from the ordinary integral of the nonnegative density. -/

/-- Points where the relative density vanishes have zero induced probability. -/

/-- Finite actual KL and the shifted logarithm integral follow from a normalized
relative density and an integrable entropy integrand. No KL identity is a premise. -/

/-- The posterior is the actual base measure tilted by `ρ/Z`. -/

/-- An ordinary positive finite normalizer constructs a posterior probability. -/

/-- The trial density relative to the original base measure. -/

/-- Composition of actual density changes gives the claimed base density. -/

/-- The ordinary log ratio agrees on the trial law's actual support. -/

/-- A genuine density-normalization bridge for the source log-density free
energy. The posterior, trial law, finite KL, and integral identity are derived.
The assumptions are density measurability, positivity, normalization and entropy
integrability; the desired variational identity is not assumed. -/

`∫ f log(f/ρ) dν`, with the actual trial density `f=rρ/Z`. Integrability of this
base-measure expression is also derived, rather than separately assumed. -/

end LatentDiffusion.Density

Consequently (u⋆,q⋆)(u_\star,q_\star)(u⋆​,q⋆​) is a global minimizer exactly when u⋆u_\staru⋆​ globally maximizes ℓ~\widetilde\ellℓ and q⋆m=πu⋆mq_\star^m=\pi_{u_\star}^mq⋆m​=πu⋆​m​ for every datum. The occurrence of z0:Kz_{0:K}z0:K​ in the proposition's normalizer is inconsistent with that definition. Positivity, finiteness, admissibility and integrability are explicit here. On the paper's P2\mathcal P_2P2​ domain the normalized posteriors must in particular have finite second moments; positive finite normalizers alone do not guarantee this. /-! # The normalized variational problem

The free energy is defined by its canonical normalized form, minus log evidence
plus average actual KL divergence. Admissibility retains finite KL before any
`toReal` conversion. Identifying this definition with a density integral needs
the usual log-integrability and normalization identities; those are not inferred
from pointwise smoothness. The theorem is valid for arbitrary measurable latent
spaces and arbitrary parameter sets, so in particular for tilted latent models.
-/

finite integrability domain. -/

Gibbs' equality theorem for actual finite measures. -/

Along the supplied finite-KL path it additionally requires continuity of the energy gap EEE, dissipation E′=−IE'=-IE′=−I, I≥0I\ge0I≥0, and the first-order transport estimate E≤I r−λr2/2E\le\sqrt I\,r-\lambda r^2/2E≤I​r−λr2/2. These give precisely the displayed parameter rate.

Its literal quantification over all P2\mathcal P_2P2​ initial laws is contradicted by Dirac laws. Entropy differentiation and transport control need the explicit analytic hypotheses above. The averaged joint potential is strongly convex in the normalized product norm ∥u∥2+M−1∑m∥zm∥2\|u\|^2+M^{-1}\sum_m\|z^m\|^2∥u∥2+M−1∑m​∥zm∥2; the sketch at main lines 168–174 must use that norm when retaining the constant λ\lambdaλ.

Formal scope. Lean proves existence and uniqueness of the actual marginal optimizer from joint convexity, and the sharp parameter rate conditional on the displayed entropy and transport bridges. Those bridges and the PDE flow are not derived from raw A1–A3. The full Wasserstein-state conclusion is a separate source claim below.

Let M>0M>0M>0, and let each datum potential UmU_mUm​ be differentiable and λ\lambdaλ-strongly convex in the full Euclidean parameter–latent pair, λ>0\lambda>0λ>0. Define the actual marginal potential

V(a)=−1M∑m=1Mlog⁡∫Rdze−Um(a,z) dz.V(a)=-\frac1M\sum_{m=1}^M\log\int_{\mathbb R^{d_z}}e^{-U_m(a,z)}\,\mathrm dz.V(a)=−M1​m=1∑M​log∫Rdz​​e−Um​(a,z)dz.

Then VVV is λ\lambdaλ-strongly convex and coercive, and has a unique global minimizer. Consequently, the actual average log evidence −V-V−V has a unique maximizer.

For a supplied posterior family satisfying the explicit identity ℓ=−V\ell=-Vℓ=−V, there is a unique joint variational optimizer (a⋆,q⋆)(a_\star,q_\star)(a⋆​,q⋆​), with q⋆m=πa⋆mq_\star^m=\pi_{a_\star}^mq⋆m​=πa⋆​m​. Normalization and identification of the supplied posteriors with the datum densities remain part of that model interpretation.

Checked endpoint — Continuous theorem, decay component — Parameter and posterior convergence

Under C1, completing a square gives the extended log-Sobolev bound and right-sided Grönwall gives

2λE(t)≤I(t)(0≤t<T),E(t)≤E(0)e−2λt(0≤t≤T).2\lambda E(t)\le I(t)\quad(0\le t<T),\qquad E(t)\le E(0)e^{-2\lambda t}\quad(0\le t\le T).2λE(t)≤I(t)(0≤t<T),E(t)≤E(0)e−2λt(0≤t≤T).

Under the marginal optimizer hypotheses above, put F⋆=F(a⋆,πa⋆)F_\star=\mathcal F(a_\star,\pi_{a_\star})F⋆​=F(a⋆​,πa⋆​​). The actual posterior KL and parameter error obey

∥at−a⋆∥≤2E(0)λ e−λt.\|a_t-a_\star\|\le\sqrt{\frac{2E(0)}\lambda}\,e^{-\lambda t}.∥at​−a⋆​∥≤λ2E(0)​​e−λt.

The sharp prefactor follows from quadratic growth of the actual marginal potential, which is proved from joint strong convexity rather than supplied as a Talagrand premise. The dissipation and first-order transport bridges C1 remain explicit; constructing the Wasserstein gradient flow and proving its entropy calculus from the source regularity alone remain outside this endpoint.

Exact statement as printed in the paper
\begin{theorem}\label{thm:exp_convg_informal}
Suppose Assumptions \Cref{assump:model_reg}-\Cref{assump:strong_log_concave} hold, then $\tilde{\ell}$ has a unique maximizer $(\theta_\star, \phi_\star)$ and the flow converges exponentially fast to it: for $\lambda$ independent of $M$ and all $t\geq 0$, 
\begin{align*}
        \vert\vert(\theta_t,\phi_t)-(\theta_\star,\phi_\star) \vert\vert
        \leq
        \sqrt{\frac{2[\tilde{F}(\theta_0, \phi_0, q_0^{1:M})-\tilde{F}_\star]}{\lambda}}e^{-\lambda t},
\end{align*}
where we denote $\tilde{F}_\star:=\inf_{(\theta,\phi,q^{1:M})}\tilde{F}(\theta,\phi,q^{1:M})$ and $\vert\vert\cdot\vert\vert$ denotes the Euclidean norm.
\end{theorem}

thrm:error-bound · main_aistats.tex:208–212

Partial formalization: the Lean code proves the stated endpoint or supporting component; the complete source statement remains unproved.

Mathematical statement

For the full-batch exact-gradient Euler–Maruyama recursion in eq:disc_theta–eq:disc_par, the source assumes A1–A4 and Lipschitz gradients of RRR. For sufficiently small h>0h>0h>0 it states

(E∥uTN,h−u⋆∥2)1/2≤Ch,N+CρT,Ch,N=O(h+N−1/2),T∈N.\bigl(\mathbb E\|u_T^{N,h}-u_\star\|^2\bigr)^{1/2} \le C_{h,N}+C\rho^T,\qquad C_{h,N}=O(\sqrt h+N^{-1/2}),\quad T\in\mathbb N.(E∥uTN,h​−u⋆​∥2)1/2≤Ch,N​+CρT,Ch,N​=O(h​+N−1/2),T∈N.

Here Ch,NC_{h,N}Ch,N​ is independent of TTT, CCC is independent of (h,N,T)(h,N,T)(h,N,T), and 0<ρ<10\lt\rho\lt10<ρ<1 may depend on hhh. Writing the transient as e−λhTe^{-\lambda hT}e−λhT makes the dependence on physical time explicit. Uniform constants require the stated initialization and moment controls.

Correction / required qualification.The temporal lemma contains an extra square-root factor; its corrected general estimate is ChC\sqrt hCh​, not the O(h)O(h)O(h) accidentally written there. The empirical comparison needs a specified coupling, and the spatial comparison needs compatible initialization and uniform moments. This theorem concerns the full batch method, as the paper itself states at main line 314. It gives no guarantee for Algorithm 1's changed minibatch temperature or the adaptive algorithm.

Formal scope. The coordinate recursion and cloud geometry are checked. A new explicit RMS theorem is proved under an integral reference, moment, residual and oracle hypotheses, and is presented in the new-theory part. It is not a recovery of this source theorem from raw A1–A4; the required stochastic reference construction remains open.

Theorem New 1 below gives an explicit conditional numerical analogue. Its reference and moment hypotheses are listed in Part II; it is not a reconstruction from A1–A4.

\begin{theorem}\label{thrm:error-bound}
Suppose that the premise of Theorem~\ref{thm:exp_convg_informal} and \Cref{assump:lipschitz_grad} hold, and that $\mathcal{R}$ has Lipschitz gradients. For all sufficiently small $h>0$, there exists a constant $C_{h,N}$ of order $\mathcal{O}(h^{1/2}+N^{-1/2})$ independent of $T$, a $\rho \in (0, 1)$, and a $C>0$ independent of $(h,N,T)$, such that
$$\mathbb{E}\left[\vert\vert(\theta_T,\phi_T)-(\theta_\star,\phi_\star) \vert\vert^2\right]^{1/2} \leq C_{h,N}+C\rho^T\quad\forall T\in \mathbb{N},$$
where $(\theta_\star,\phi_\star)$ denote $\tilde{\ell}$'s unique maximizer.
\end{theorem}

/-!
# Additional source results, on their explicit mathematical domains

These theorems reconstruct elementary steps used in the supplied manuscript.
They do not construct optimal transport plans, identify a Wasserstein metric
derivative, or justify differentiation or integration by parts on an unbounded
domain. Those continuum application steps remain separate obligations.

`cauchy_minimizing_sequence` corrects Supplement `lem:cauchy`: a Cauchy
sequence must also be a minimizing sequence. A complete ambient metric space
and lower semicontinuity then give an actual minimizer.
-/

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory Set Filter
open scoped Topology

namespace LatentDiffusion.SourceResults

/-- Corrected Supplement `lem:cauchy`: completeness and lower semicontinuity
identify the limit of a Cauchy *minimizing* sequence as a minimizer.
No unrelated Cauchy sequence supplies this conclusion. -/

/-- The scalar derivative used in Supplement `app:lemma_1st_var` includes
the additive constant one. It disappears only on zero-total-mass directions. -/

/-- Constants represent the same first variation on probability tangent
directions. This proves the precise reason the source may omit `+1`. -/

/-- The source's normalized product metric cancels the `1/M` from the
distributional first variation with the inverse metric's `M`.
The positivity of the data count is essential. -/

/-- The first-order scalar consequence of the source's geodesic-convexity
inequality. This step is proved by taking the right derivative; the existence
and calculus of an actual Wasserstein geodesic is not a premise hidden here. -/

/-- The source's Talagrand-type quadratic growth follows directly from strong
geodesic convexity at a minimizer. This proof needs no entropy dissipation.
The application must still establish the displayed convexity inequality for
its actual displacement interpolation and actual metric distance. -/

/-- The actual tilted density in main-text `eq:ptildedef`. -/

/-- The log-density free energy used by the paper, relative to a base measure. -/

/-- Pointwise tilt identity, including zeros of the trial density. -/

/-- Main-text free-energy decomposition after `eq:free-energy`, proved for
the actual base-density integral. Both integrable summands are explicit. -/

/-- Nonnegative KL regularization raises the density free energy. The KL
interpretation of `R` is independent of this integral inequality. -/

/-- Integrability and evidence order follow from a nonnegative integrable
base density and a measurable nonnegative penalty, as used after main-text
`eq:ptildedef`. The tilted integral is not assumed integrable in advance. -/

/-- Taking logs preserves the source's evidence comparison when the tilted
normalizer is positive. Its positivity must be established for the model. -/

/-- Exact finite uniform expectation over the diffusion time index. This is
the arithmetic mean on `Fin K`, so no sampling or asymptotic premise is used. -/

/-- Supplement `app_eq:diffusion_likelihood` and
`app:one_sample_simplified_diffusion`: without inverse-inclusion scaling,
a uniformly selected summand estimates the average, rather than the sum. -/

/-- Corrected unbiased single-time estimator of a *summed* diffusion
objective: multiply the sampled summand by the number of time indices. -/

end LatentDiffusion.SourceResults

/-!
# Dominated first variations of the actual density free-energy integral

Source: `papers/Latent_diffusion/supp_aistats.tex:188–199`,
Lemma `app:lemma_1st_var`.

The parameter result differentiates the actual integral, using pointwise
Fréchet derivatives and one integrable domination bound on a common parameter
neighborhood. The density result differentiates the actual integral along
`q + t r`, using positivity and integrable derivative domination on a common
interval. Neither result assumes the desired integral derivative.

These domination/integrability conditions are additional explicit analytic
hypotheses; the paper's A1 does not by itself establish them. The `+1` in the
ordinary entropy derivative disappears on zero-mass density perturbations.
No Wasserstein gradient, PDE integration by parts or flow construction is
claimed by this module.
-/

noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory Filter
open scoped Topology

namespace LatentDiffusion.SourceCalculus

variable {Z A : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Z]
  [NormedAddCommGroup A] [NormedSpace ℝ A]

/-- The actual base-density free energy with potential `U = -log ρ`. -/

/-- Parameter differentiation in source Lemma `app:lemma_1st_var`, with an
explicit weighted derivative bound that justifies differentiation under the
integral. The density is held fixed. In the source, use
`U(θ,φ,z) = L_D(θ,z) - log p_φ(x|z)` and split its derivative. -/

/-- The ordinary pointwise derivative along an affine density perturbation.
This is used below inside a dominated differentiation theorem. -/

/-- Genuine density-direction differentiation of the source free-energy
integral. Positivity and the domination bound hold on one common neighborhood
of zero, rather than point-dependent neighborhoods. -/

/-- On probability-density tangent directions the constant `+1` vanishes.
The conclusion is the source's density first variation, now for an actual
integral with all dominated-differentiation hypotheses exposed. -/

end LatentDiffusion.SourceCalculus

Exact statement as printed in the paper
\begin{lemma}\label{app:lemma_1st_var}
     Given the free energy of the form in \eqref{eq_app:decomposed_obj}:
\begin{equation}
    \tilde{F}(\theta, \phi, q)  =  \int \mathcal{L}_D(\theta, z) q(z)\dd z - \int \log \left(\frac{p_\phi( x|z)}{q(z)}\right) q(z)\dd z.
\end{equation}
The first variation $\delta \tilde{F}(\theta, \phi, q)=(\delta_q \tilde{F}(\theta, \phi, q), \delta_\theta \tilde{F}(\theta, \phi, q), \delta_\phi \tilde{F}(\theta, \phi, q))$ is given by:
\begin{align}
    \delta_q \tilde{F}(\theta, \phi, q) &= \log \left(\frac{q(z)}{p_\phi( x|z)}\right) + \mathcal{L}_D(\theta, z)\label{eq_app:1st_var_q}   \\
    \delta_\theta \tilde{F}(\theta, \phi, q) &= \int \nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}_D(\theta, z) q(z) \dd z\label{eq_app:1st_var_theta}  \\
    \delta_\phi \tilde{F}(\theta, \phi, q) &= - \int \nabla_\phi \log p_\phi( x|z) q(z) \dd z\label{eq_app:1st_var_phi} 
\end{align}
\end{lemma}

Equip the product state with d2((u,q),(v,r))=∥u−v∥2+M−1∑mW2(qm,rm)2d^2((u,q),(v,r))=\|u-v\|^2+M^{-1}\sum_mW_2(q^m,r^m)^2d2((u,q),(v,r))=∥u−v∥2+M−1∑m​W2​(qm,rm)2, and let Vum=LD(θ,⋅)−log⁡pϕ(xm∣⋅)V_u^m=\mathcal L_D(\theta,\cdot)-\log p_\phi(x^m\mid\cdot)Vum​=LD​(θ,⋅)−logpϕ​(xm∣⋅). Wherever the first variations and Otto metric representation are justified, the parameter and density gradients are

∇uF~=1M∑m∫∇uVum dqm,∇qmF~=−∇z ⁣⋅(qm∇z(log⁡qm+Vum)).\nabla_u\widetilde F=\frac1M\sum_m\int\nabla_u V_u^m\,dq^m, \qquad \nabla_{q^m}\widetilde F=-\nabla_z\!\cdot \bigl(q^m\nabla_z(\log q^m+V_u^m)\bigr).∇u​F=M1​m∑​∫∇u​Vum​dqm,∇qm​F=−∇z​⋅(qm∇z​(logqm+Vum​)).

Thus the descent flow has u˙=−M−1∑m∫∇uVum dqm\dot u=-M^{-1}\sum_m\int\nabla_uV_u^m\,dq^mu˙=−M−1∑m​∫∇u​Vum​dqm and ∂tqm=∇z⋅(qm∇zVum)+Δqm\partial_tq^m=\nabla_z\cdot(q^m\nabla_zV_u^m)+\Delta q^m∂t​qm=∇z​⋅(qm∇z​Vum​)+Δqm.

Correction / required qualification.The inverse metric in each law block contributes MMM, cancelling the objective's 1/M1/M1/M. There is consequently no additional 1/M1/M1/M in the density drift or diffusion. These formulas use the descent loss VVV, avoiding the inconsistent concise-loss sign in main lines 222–226.

Formal scope. SourceResults proves the exact M-times-inverse-M cancellation for any real module and positive data count. The full-cloud finite-dimensional coordinate identities are checked separately. This factor calculation does not construct the continuum Wasserstein tangent metric or its gradient, which remain unproved.

\begin{proposition}
    Under the normalized product geometry of \Cref{app:metric}, the gradients of the averaged free energy $\tilde{F}(\theta, \phi, q^{1:M})$ with respect to $(\theta, \phi, q^{1:M})$ are given by:
    \begin{align}
    \nabla_\theta \tilde{F}(\theta, \phi, q^{1:M}) &= \frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^M \int \left[\nabla_{\theta} \mathcal{L}_D(\theta, z)\right] q^m(z) \dd z \\
    \nabla_\phi \tilde{F}(\theta, \phi, q^{1:M}) &= -\frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^M \int \left[\nabla_{\phi} \log p_{\phi}( x^m | z)\right] q^m(z) \dd z \\
    \nabla_{q^m} \tilde{F}(\theta, \phi, q^{1:M}) &=  \nabla_{z} \cdot \left[
        q^m(z) \nabla_{z} \left[
            \log \left(
                \frac{p_{\phi}( x^m|z)}{q^m(z)}
            \right) - \mathcal{L}_D(\theta, z)
        \right]
    \right], \quad \forall m\in[M].
\end{align}
\end{proposition}

Exact statement as printed in the paper
\begin{lemma}[Geodesics on $\mathcal{M}^{1:M}$]\label{lem:geodesic}
    A curve $\gamma(t) : t \in [0, 1] \mapsto \mathcal{M}^{1:M}$ is a geodesic if and only if $\gamma(t) = (\gamma_{\theta}(t), \gamma_\phi (t), \gamma_{q^1}(t), \ldots, \gamma_{q^M}(t))$, where $\gamma_{\theta}$ and $\gamma_\phi$ are geodesics in the Euclidean parameter space and each $\gamma_{q^m}$ is a geodesic in $(\mathcal{P}_2(\sZ), \mathrm{d}_{W_2})$. In particular, if $\gamma(t)$ is a geodesic in $\mathcal{M}^{1:M}$ connecting $(\theta, \phi, q^{1:M})$ and $(\theta', \phi', (q')^{1:M})$ then 
    \begin{align*}
        \gamma_{\theta}(t) &= (1-t)\theta + t\theta', \\
        \gamma_{\phi}(t) &= (1-t)\phi + t\phi', \\
        \gamma_{q^m}(t) &= (h_t)_{\#}\varrho^m, \quad m=1,\ldots,M,
    \end{align*}
    where $\varrho^m$'s are Wasserstein-2 optimal transport plans for $(q^m, (q')^m)$ and $h_t(z,z') = (1-t)z + tz'$. Furthermore, if $q^m$'s have densities with respect to the Lebesgue measure, then we can also write:
    \begin{align*}
        \gamma_{q^m}(t) = ((1-t)\mathrm{id} + t\nabla_z f^m)_{\#} q^m, \quad \forall m \in [M],
    \end{align*}
    for some convex function $f^m$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:cauchy}
    Denote $\mathcal{M}_\star := \arg\min_{(\theta, \phi, q^{1:M}) \in \mathcal{M}^{1:M}} \tilde{F}(\theta, \phi, q^{1:M})$ as the set of minimizers of $\tilde{F}$ and $\tilde{F}_\star := \inf_{(\theta, \phi, q^{1:M}) \in \mathcal{M}^{1:M}} \tilde{F}(\theta, \phi, q^{1:M})$ as the optimal value. Under the extended log-Sobolev inequality, for a Cauchy sequence $\{(\theta_n, \phi_n, q_n^{1:M})\}_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ in $\mathcal{M}^{1:M,1}$, there exists an increasing sequence of $t_n \to +\infty$ such that:
    \begin{equation*}
        (\theta_{t_n}, \phi_{t_n}, q_{t_n}^{1:M}) \to (\theta_\star, \phi_\star, q_\star^{1:M}) \in \mathcal{M}_\star, \quad \text{as} \ n \to +\infty,
    \end{equation*}
    for some $(\theta_\star, \phi_\star, q_\star^{1:M}) \in \mathcal{M}_\star$ in the topology induced by $\mathsf{d}_{\mathcal{M}^{1:M}}$ on $\mathcal{M}^{1:M}$.
\end{lemma}

A corrected flow proof requires a consistent global flow, dissipation, the metric-speed bound, extended LSI, lower semicontinuity and the preceding complete-space minimizer argument. Correction / required qualification.The definition defn:xTalagrand at supplement lines 614–620 takes a redundant infimum over the starting state itself. If a minimizer exists, that literal right-hand side is zero. Remove this infimum and keep the given starting state fixed; the only infimum is over the minimizing set. Section-wide A1/A2 and the analytic lemmas are also used, even though the theorem's local sentence mentions only xLSI.

The full Wasserstein-flow argument remains open.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:exp_convg_appendix}
    Suppose Assumptions~\Cref{assump:model_reg}-\Cref{assump:strong_log_concave} are satisfied. Then, $\tilde{\ell}$ has a unique maximizer $(\theta_\star, \phi_\star)$ and the flow converges exponentially fast to it: for some $\lambda>0$ independent of $M$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:app_thm_exp}
        \mathsf{d}_{\mathcal{M}^{1:M}}((\theta_t,\phi_t,q_t^{1:M}),(\theta_\star,\phi_\star,q_{\star}^{1:M}))
        \leq
        \sqrt{\frac{2[\tilde{F}(\theta_t, \phi_t, q_t^{1:M}) - \tilde{F}_\star]}{\lambda}}
        \leq
        \sqrt{\frac{2[\tilde{F}(\theta_0, \phi_0, q_0^{1:M})-\tilde{F}_\star]}{\lambda}}e^{-\lambda t}, \quad \forall t>0;
\end{equation}
where $\tilde{F}_\star:=\inf_{(\theta,\phi,q^{1:M})\in \mathcal{M}^{1:M}}\tilde{F}(\theta,\phi,q^{1:M})$ and $\vert\vert\cdot\vert\vert$ denotes the Euclidean norm.
\end{theorem}

Mathematical statement

The source states strong well-posedness of the mean-field SDE and exponential convergence of its empirical clouds to target clouds. A precise fixed-time comparison is: for each datum and time ttt, choose independent particle pairs (Ztm,n,Ytm,n)(Z_t^{m,n},Y_t^{m,n})(Ztm,n​,Ytm,n​) from an optimal coupling of qtm,q⋆mq_t^m,q_\star^mqtm​,q⋆m​. With empirical laws Qtm,N,Q⋆,tm,NQ_t^{m,N},Q_{\star,t}^{m,N}Qtm,N​,Q⋆,tm,N​,

(∥ut−u⋆∥2+1M∑mEW2(Qtm,N,Q⋆,tm,N)2)1/2≤d((ut,qt),(u⋆,q⋆))≤Ce−λt.\left(\|u_t-u_\star\|^2+ \frac1M\sum_m\mathbb E W_2(Q_t^{m,N},Q_{\star,t}^{m,N})^2 \right)^{1/2} \le d((u_t,q_t),(u_\star,q_\star))\le Ce^{-\lambda t}.(∥ut​−u⋆​∥2+M1​m∑​EW2​(Qtm,N​,Q⋆,tm,N​)2)1/2≤d((ut​,qt​),(u⋆​,q⋆​))≤Ce−λt.

This coupling comparison is at a fixed time. It does not specify a single time-independent sampled target cloud for an entire trajectory.

Correction / required qualification.Arbitrary independent target samples do not satisfy the identity equating their pairwise L² cost to W₂ at supplement line 781. An optimal fixed-time coupling makes that step valid; a synchronous reference process gives a different, explicitly coupled comparison. Particles may be identically distributed across n for a fixed datum m, but different data generally have different latent laws.

Formal scope. Neither the source mean-field SDE strong-solution construction nor this optimal-coupling empirical theorem is currently proved in Lean. New numerical reference theorems assume their own integral reference rather than proving the source statement.

\begin{lemma}[Spatial Discretization Error]\label{lem:spatial_discretization}
    Suppose Assumptions~\Cref{assump:strong_log_concave} and~\Cref{assump:lipschitz_grad} hold. Then the following system of SDEs:
    \begin{align}
        \dd \tilde\theta_t^N &= \frac{1}{MN} \sum_{m=1}^{M} \sum_{n=1}^N \nabla_{\tilde\theta} \tilde{\ell}^m(\tilde\theta_t^N, \bar{Z}_t^{m,n}) \, \dd t \label{eq_app:spatial1} \\
        \dd \bar{Z}_t^{m,n} &= \nabla_{z} \tilde{\ell}^m(\tilde\theta_t^N, \bar{Z}_t^{m,n}) \, \dd t + \sqrt{2} \, \dd W_t^{m,n}, \quad (m,n)\in[M]\times [N], \label{eq_app:spatial3}
    \end{align}
    has a strong solution $(\tilde\theta_t^N, \bar{Z}_t^{1:M, 1:N})_{t \geq 0}$. Furthermore, there exists a constant $C(N)>0$ of order $\mathcal{O}(N^{-1/2})$ independent of $t$ and $M$, such that:
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathsf{d}_{\mathcal{M}^{1:M}}((\tilde\theta_t^N, \bar{Q}_t^{1:M, N}), (\tilde\theta_t, Q_t^{1:M,N})) \leq C(N), \quad \forall t>0,
    \end{equation*}
    where $\bar{Q}_t^{m, N}:=N^{-1}\sum_{n=1}^N \delta_{\bar{Z}_t^{m,n}}$ for each $m\in [M]$ and $Q_t^{m,N}$ is defined as in Lemma~\ref{lem:cont-time-convg}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Temporal Discretization Error]\label{lem:temporal_discretization}
    Suppose Assumptions~\Cref{assump:strong_log_concave} and~\Cref{assump:lipschitz_grad} hold. Then for the following Euler-Maruyama scheme for the SDEs in \eqref{eq_app:spatial1}-\eqref{eq_app:spatial3}:
    \begin{align}
        \tilde\theta_{k+1}^{N,h} &= \tilde\theta_k^{N,h} + \frac{h}{MN} \sum_{m=1}^{M}\sum_{n=1}^N \nabla_{\tilde\theta} \tilde{\ell}(\tilde\theta_k^{N,h}, \bar{Z}_k^{m,n,N,h}) \label{eq_app:temp1} \\
        \bar{Z}_{k+1}^{m,n,N,h} &= \bar{Z}_k^{m,n,N,h} + h \nabla_{z} \tilde{\ell}(\tilde\theta_k^{N,h}, \bar{Z}_k^{m,n,N,h}) + \sqrt{2h} W_k^n, \quad (m,n) \in [M] \times [N], \label{eq_app:temp3}
    \end{align}
    we have for $h \leq {1}/({\lambda+L})$ with $\lambda$ being the strong concavity constant in Assumption~\Cref{assump:strong_log_concave} and $L$ being the Lipschitz constant in \Cref{assump:lipschitz_grad}, there exists a constant $C(h)>0$ independent of $k$ and $N$ of order $\mathcal{O}(h^{1/2})$,
    such that:
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathsf{d}_{\mathcal{M}^{1:M}}((\tilde\theta_k^{N,h}, \bar{Q}_k^{1:M,N,h}), (\tilde\theta_{kh}^N, \bar{Q}_{kh}^{1:M,N})) \leq \sqrt{h}C(h), \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N},
    \end{equation*}
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}\label{thrm_app:error-bound}
Suppose that the premise of Theorem~\ref{thm:exp_convg_informal} and \Cref{assump:lipschitz_grad} hold, and that $\mathcal{R}$ has Lipschitz gradients. For all sufficiently small $h>0$, there exists an $\mathcal{O}(h^{1/2}+N^{-1/2})$ constant $C_{h,N}$ independent of $T$, a $\rho \in (0, 1)$, and a $C>0$ independent of $(h,N,T)$, such that
$$\mathbb{E}\left[\vert\vert\tilde\theta_T-\tilde\theta_\star \vert\vert^2\right]^{1/2} \leq C_{h,N}+C\rho^T\quad\forall T\in \mathbb{N},$$
where $\tilde\theta_\star$ denotes $\tilde{\ell}$'s unique maximizer.
\end{theorem}

Mathematical statement
A2 includes every finite-second-moment initial law and requires a smooth density at t=0t=0t=0. A Dirac law has finite second moment but cannot have a density relative to nonatomic Lebesgue measure. Restrict the initial class to the required smooth densities, or require smoothing only for t>0t>0t>0 and continuity in W2W_2W2​ at zero. Merely restricting to absolutely continuous laws still permits discontinuous initial densities. The Dirac obstruction is proved; the repaired flow existence theorem is an outstanding analytic task.

import LatentDiffusion.SourceAssumptions
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.WithDensity
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.Basic

/-!
# The literal time-zero solution assumption has an obstruction

An arbitrary finite-second-moment initial law includes a Dirac measure. Such a
law cannot have a density relative to a reference measure that assigns zero mass
to the corresponding singleton. This argument needs no PDE or positivity
assumption. In particular it applies to Lebesgue measure in positive dimension.
-/

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory Set

namespace LatentDiffusion.SourceObstruction

variable {P Z : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup P] [NormedSpace ℝ P]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Z] [NormedSpace ℝ Z]
  [MeasurableSpace Z] [MeasurableSingletonClass Z]

/-- The source's universal solution regularity is impossible whenever the
reference measure has even one null singleton. The initial law is an actual
finite-second-moment Dirac probability measure. -/

/-- Atomless reference measures, including positive-dimensional Lebesgue
measures, therefore rule out the literal source premise. -/

end LatentDiffusion.SourceObstruction

Corrected source claim

Zero tilt at the tilted optimum does not identify the original optimum

discussion following prop:ftildemins · main_aistats.tex:107–110

Counterexample and sufficient comparator proved in Lean

Mathematical statement
The pointwise comparison ℓ~≤ℓ\widetilde\ell\le\ellℓ≤ℓ and equality at a tilted maximizer do not imply that this point maximizes ℓ\ellℓ. On two points take log likelihoods (0,1)(0,1)(0,1) and nonnegative gaps (0,2)(0,2)(0,2): the tilted objective (0,−1)(0,-1)(0,−1) is maximized at the zero-gap point, but the original objective is maximized at the other point. A sufficient corrected condition is that an original-objective maximizer has zero gap; then every tilted maximizer attains the original optimal value. Uniform zero penalty across the whole model also suffices.

/-! # The normalized variational problem

The free energy is defined by its canonical normalized form, minus log evidence
plus average actual KL divergence. Admissibility retains finite KL before any
`toReal` conversion. Identifying this definition with a density integral needs
the usual log-integrability and normalization identities; those are not inferred
from pointwise smoothness. The theorem is valid for arbitrary measurable latent
spaces and arbitrary parameter sets, so in particular for tilted latent models.
-/
noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory
open scoped BigOperators ENNReal
namespace LatentDiffusion

variable {A Z : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Z] {M : ℕ}

/-- The tilted log evidence and its normalized posterior at each datum. -/

namespace PosteriorFamily
variable (P : PosteriorFamily A Z M)

/-- Excludes infinite entropy from real arithmetic. -/

/-- The normalized free energy, equal to the log-density definition on its
finite integrability domain. -/





/-- Equality in the variational bound identifies every posterior, using
Gibbs' equality theorem for actual finite measures. -/

/-- Proposition 1, including the unique optimal variational distribution.
No existence of a log-evidence maximizer is assumed or concluded. -/

end PosteriorFamily

/-- The valid zero-tilt comparison requires a true optimum attaining zero
gap. Zero gap only at a tilted optimum is insufficient. -/

/-- A zero-penalty tilted maximizer can fail to maximize the true likelihood.
Both likelihoods and gaps here are exact real numbers on a two-point model. -/

end LatentDiffusion

/-!
# Exact mini-batch noise and temperature audit

For one fixed datum, a uniform batch of size B among M data has inclusion
probability p = B/M. Algorithm 1 uses an inverse-inclusion drift h/p when the

The calculations below integrate the actual standard Gaussian; no diffusion
limit or invariant-law assumption is used. In particular, the source's claimed
variance matching fails even for the one-dimensional quadratic potential.

The scalar moment chains are defined recursions, derived from the exact
one-step conditional Gaussian moment. They do not assert existence or
convergence of a nonlinear adaptive Adam sampler.
-/

/-- Corrected Supplement `lem:cauchy`: completeness and lower semicontinuity
identify the limit of a Cauchy *minimizing* sequence as a minimizer.
No unrelated Cauchy sequence supplies this conclusion. -/

/-- The scalar derivative used in Supplement `app:lemma_1st_var` includes
the additive constant one. It disappears only on zero-total-mass directions. -/

/-- Constants represent the same first variation on probability tangent
directions. This proves the precise reason the source may omit `+1`. -/

/-- The source's normalized product metric cancels the `1/M` from the
distributional first variation with the inverse metric's `M`.
The positivity of the data count is essential. -/

/-- The first-order scalar consequence of the source's geodesic-convexity
inequality. This step is proved by taking the right derivative; the existence
and calculus of an actual Wasserstein geodesic is not a premise hidden here. -/

/-- The source's Talagrand-type quadratic growth follows directly from strong
geodesic convexity at a minimizer. This proof needs no entropy dissipation.
The application must still establish the displayed convexity inequality for
its actual displacement interpolation and actual metric distance. -/

/-- The actual tilted density in main-text `eq:ptildedef`. -/

/-- The log-density free energy used by the paper, relative to a base measure. -/

/-- Pointwise tilt identity, including zeros of the trial density. -/

/-- Main-text free-energy decomposition after `eq:free-energy`, proved for
the actual base-density integral. Both integrable summands are explicit. -/

/-- Nonnegative KL regularization raises the density free energy. The KL
interpretation of `R` is independent of this integral inequality. -/

/-- Integrability and evidence order follow from a nonnegative integrable
base density and a measurable nonnegative penalty, as used after main-text
`eq:ptildedef`. The tilted integral is not assumed integrable in advance. -/

/-- Taking logs preserves the source's evidence comparison when the tilted
normalizer is positive. Its positivity must be established for the model. -/

/-- Exact finite uniform expectation over the diffusion time index. This is
the arithmetic mean on `Fin K`, so no sampling or asymptotic premise is used. -/

/-- Supplement `app_eq:diffusion_likelihood` and
`app:one_sample_simplified_diffusion`: without inverse-inclusion scaling,
a uniformly selected summand estimates the average, rather than the sum. -/

/-- Corrected unbiased single-time estimator of a *summed* diffusion
objective: multiply the sampled summand by the number of time indices. -/

end LatentDiffusion.SourceResults

The Cauchy sequence in the printed lemma is unrelated to the flow. It must be a flow sequence atna_{t_n}atn​​, with tn↑∞t_n\uparrow\inftytn​↑∞ and energy tending to the infimum. The lower-semicontinuity proof separately uses joint continuity of RRR; nonnegative joint lower semicontinuity is a sufficient explicit replacement. The xLSI proof's chosen minimizer must also be constructed before it is used.

Mathematical statement
Pointwise smoothness and finite second moments alone do not ensure finite positive entropy, finite Fisher information, an integrable time derivative, vanishing boundary terms or integrable transport-gradient pairings. The source's first-variation, de Bruijn and initial-geodesic-derivative arguments need those hypotheses or a proved approximation argument. For distance to a fixed point, use a metric derivative almost everywhere or an upper-Dini derivative, since an ordinary distance derivative may fail at a crossing time.
Exact Lean contract

/-!
# Dominated first variations of the actual density free-energy integral

Source: `papers/Latent_diffusion/supp_aistats.tex:188–199`,
Lemma `app:lemma_1st_var`.

The parameter result differentiates the actual integral, using pointwise
Fréchet derivatives and one integrable domination bound on a common parameter
neighborhood. The density result differentiates the actual integral along
`q + t r`, using positivity and integrable derivative domination on a common
interval. Neither result assumes the desired integral derivative.

These domination/integrability conditions are additional explicit analytic
hypotheses; the paper's A1 does not by itself establish them. The `+1` in the
ordinary entropy derivative disappears on zero-mass density perturbations.
No Wasserstein gradient, PDE integration by parts or flow construction is
claimed by this module.
-/

/-!
# Additional source results, on their explicit mathematical domains

These theorems reconstruct elementary steps used in the supplied manuscript.
They do not construct optimal transport plans, identify a Wasserstein metric
derivative, or justify differentiation or integration by parts on an unbounded
domain. Those continuum application steps remain separate obligations.

`cauchy_minimizing_sequence` corrects Supplement `lem:cauchy`: a Cauchy
sequence must also be a minimizing sequence. A complete ambient metric space
and lower semicontinuity then give an actual minimizer.
-/

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory Set Filter
open scoped Topology

namespace LatentDiffusion.SourceResults

/-- Corrected Supplement `lem:cauchy`: completeness and lower semicontinuity
identify the limit of a Cauchy *minimizing* sequence as a minimizer.
No unrelated Cauchy sequence supplies this conclusion. -/

/-- The scalar derivative used in Supplement `app:lemma_1st_var` includes
the additive constant one. It disappears only on zero-total-mass directions. -/

/-- Constants represent the same first variation on probability tangent
directions. This proves the precise reason the source may omit `+1`. -/

/-- The source's normalized product metric cancels the `1/M` from the
distributional first variation with the inverse metric's `M`.
The positivity of the data count is essential. -/

/-- The first-order scalar consequence of the source's geodesic-convexity
inequality. This step is proved by taking the right derivative; the existence
and calculus of an actual Wasserstein geodesic is not a premise hidden here. -/

/-- The source's Talagrand-type quadratic growth follows directly from strong
geodesic convexity at a minimizer. This proof needs no entropy dissipation.
The application must still establish the displayed convexity inequality for
its actual displacement interpolation and actual metric distance. -/

/-- The actual tilted density in main-text `eq:ptildedef`. -/

/-- The log-density free energy used by the paper, relative to a base measure. -/

/-- Pointwise tilt identity, including zeros of the trial density. -/

/-- Main-text free-energy decomposition after `eq:free-energy`, proved for
the actual base-density integral. Both integrable summands are explicit. -/

/-- Nonnegative KL regularization raises the density free energy. The KL
interpretation of `R` is independent of this integral inequality. -/

/-- Integrability and evidence order follow from a nonnegative integrable
base density and a measurable nonnegative penalty, as used after main-text
`eq:ptildedef`. The tilted integral is not assumed integrable in advance. -/

/-- Taking logs preserves the source's evidence comparison when the tilted
normalizer is positive. Its positivity must be established for the model. -/

/-- Exact finite uniform expectation over the diffusion time index. This is
the arithmetic mean on `Fin K`, so no sampling or asymptotic premise is used. -/

/-- Supplement `app_eq:diffusion_likelihood` and
`app:one_sample_simplified_diffusion`: without inverse-inclusion scaling,
a uniformly selected summand estimates the average, rather than the sum. -/

/-- Corrected unbiased single-time estimator of a *summed* diffusion
objective: multiply the sampled summand by the number of time indices. -/

end LatentDiffusion.SourceResults

The concise update subtracts gradients but defines its loss from Lm=log⁡pϕ−LD\mathcal L^m=\log p_\phi-\mathcal L_DLm=logpϕ​−LD​, the opposite of the loss used by the following minibatch equation. Define the descent loss as Vm=LD−log⁡pϕV^m=\mathcal L_D-\log p_\phiVm=LD​−logpϕ​; then the full-batch parameter and particle updates subtract its gradients, with the particle factor MNMNMN applied to the averaged loss. independent parameter and latent dimensions. -/

/-- Extract the scaled latent vector of particle `i`. -/

/-- The actual positive drift force in particle-normalized coordinates.

with an individual datum-particle force and no extra factor of `M` or `N`. -/

end LatentDiffusion.Cloud

The momentum tracks the positive gradient of the descent loss, but the particle update adds it. With that momentum convention, descent requires −hzGM-h_zGM−hz​GM. The loop's particle index is B×[N]\mathcal B\times[N]B×[N], not B×[M]\mathcal B\times[M]B×[M]. The equation scales noise variance by 1/M1/M1/M, and the implementation paragraph adds a further noise-amplitude factor 1/B1/B1/B; these change the sampler. The pseudocode also overwrites its drifted temporary value when adding noise, so the intended update should add drift and noise to the same new state. For a state-dependent preconditioner a target-preserving Langevin diffusion generally needs the appropriate divergence drift; momentum requires an enlarged-state invariant-law analysis. None of these changes is covered by the source's full-batch theorem.

Part II — New theory

The paper already gives a full-batch error rate with implicit constants. These additions make the force geometry, particle variance, discretization and oracle contributions explicit. Their hypotheses are listed first.

What changes for inference?

The final bound separates initialization, particle count, step size and oracle noise, so each source of parameter error can be budgeted.

What changes for minibatches?

Exact variance and scalar temperature calculations distinguish sampling error from a change of target caused by the printed noise scaling.

What changes for model bias?

A one-sided evidence gap turns approximate tilted optimization into an explicit distance from the original model’s optimizer.

New Assumptions — N1–N7

N1 is the force interface, derived from A3–A4 for the scaled cloud. N2 is the step restriction. N3–N4 describe alternative reference formulations; N5–N7 supply the probabilistic inputs for the main bound. Each theorem below names the subset it uses; these premises are not asserted to follow from A1–A4.

New theory

N1 — Monotone, Lipschitz force

Mathematical statement

Let HHH be a real inner-product space. The positive force FFF, equal to minus the drift, satisfies for every x,y∈Hx,y\in Hx,y∈H

λ∥x−y∥2≤⟨F(x)−F(y),x−y⟩,∥F(x)−F(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,L≥0.\lambda\|x-y\|^2\le\langle F(x)-F(y),x-y\rangle,\qquad \|F(x)-F(y)\|\le L\|x-y\|,\quad L\ge0.λ∥x−y∥2≤⟨F(x)−F(y),x−y⟩,∥F(x)−F(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,L≥0.

This is an explicit assumption on the complete force of the parameter and particle system in the chosen norm. Applying a per-datapoint hypothesis to that complete system requires its own lifting argument.

ForceRegularity · definition and context

Exact shared Lean context
import UnadjustedLangevin.GradientStep
import UnadjustedLangevin.Recurrence
import UnadjustedLangevin.LocalError
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Exp
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.L2Space

/-!
# Quantitative stability and discretization error for latent Euler algorithms

These results concern actual Euler updates on a real inner product space.  In the
paper's interacting algorithm that space can be the latent parameter / particle
cloud with its particle-normalized inner product.  Neither contraction nor an
error recurrence is included among the hypotheses.

The reference-path consistency hypothesis below is a *local defect bound*.  An
SDE application must establish it from the drift and Brownian regularity; this
file does not claim that such a bound follows from monotonicity alone.
-/

open scoped NNReal

namespace LatentDiffusion

variable {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]

/-- Added regularity assumption on the positive force, i.e. minus the SDE drift.
The constant `L` is nonnegative by its type. -/

/-- A step restriction stated without division, including degenerate spaces. -/

/-- The Euler update, with the entire additive noise increment supplied as `ξ`.
For IPLD it is `sqrt (2h)` times the appropriately scaled Gaussian cloud. -/

/-- The actual numerical trajectory, rather than an assumed error recurrence. -/

/-- Shared additive noise cancels, and strong monotonicity yields the sharp
quadratic one-step coefficient. -/

/-- A simpler squared contraction with a transparent step restriction. -/

/-- Norm contraction sufficient for robust coupling and numerical consistency. -/

/-- The familiar minimum step restriction implies the division-free one. -/

/-- A single update separates force approximation error from the reference's
local discretization defect. No stochastic independence is required. -/

/-- Finite-horizon robust numerical bound, including the exact geometric factor.
`G` is the implemented force; `F` is the reference force. The reference can be an
exact SDE skeleton once the stated local defect estimate has been established. -/

/-- Uniform numerical and model bias: `2 B / m + (2 D / m) sqrt h`.
The dimension and number of particles do not enter this algebraic estimate. -/

end LatentDiffusion

namespace LatentDiffusion

variable {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]

/-- Squared coupling error averaged over a finite probability space. -/

/-- Explicit finite probability weights. Normalization gives the expression its
usual expectation interpretation; the algebraic estimates only need positivity. -/

/-- Euler with a shared additive increment and an additional stochastic force
innovation `ζ`, multiplied by the step size. -/

/-- The zero cross moment needed from a centered innovation is stated on the
current Euler displacement. Conditional mean zero given the current states and
shared increment is a sufficient probabilistic condition for this assumption. -/

/-- Pythagorean identity after averaging: only the explicit cross moment is used. -/

/-- Centered stochastic force error has a mean-square floor of order `h`, rather
than the order-one floor for an arbitrary bounded force error. The result is for
actual coupled Euler recursions on any finite probability space. -/

end LatentDiffusion

namespace LatentDiffusion

open MeasureTheory

variable {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H]

/-- Primitive assumptions on exact integral reference segments. In an `L²`
realization `G` bounds the drift root mean square and `N sqrt t` bounds the
Brownian-increment root mean square. These are moment assumptions, not a local
numerical error or contraction assumption. `W` is the additive noise path. -/

/-- The local consistency bound is derived from the exact integral equation,
the drift moment bound, and the square-root noise increment bound. -/

/-- Nonasymptotic Euler error derived from primitive integral-path moment bounds,
with separate numerical bias `O(h G + N sqrt h)` and force-model bias `O(B)`.
The ambient space can be an `L²` Hilbert space, in which case this is an RMS
coupling estimate. An SDE existence theorem and verification of its stated
moment and lifted-force assumptions are separate obligations. -/

end LatentDiffusion

namespace LatentDiffusion

variable {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]

/-- Centered local force innovations in a Hilbert space. On `L²(Ω,P;E)`, the
orthogonality field is exactly a zero expected cross term, and the variance
field is a second-moment bound on the stochastic force innovation. -/

/-- Uniform second-moment stability for centered stochastic force errors in an
arbitrary real Hilbert space, including genuine `L²` probability spaces. -/

section ArbitraryProbability

open MeasureTheory

variable {Ω E : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]

/-- Actual expectation interpretation of the Hilbert squared norm. `Lp` ensures
square integrability of every variable; no totalized nonintegrable expectation
is used as an error metric. -/

/-- Nonasymptotic mean-square stochastic-oracle bound on an arbitrary probability
space, permitting Gaussian innovations. `F` is the explicitly supplied force
on actual `L²` random variables and its monotonicity/Lipschitz assumptions must
hold in `L²`; pointwise cloud assumptions can be lifted separately. -/

end ArbitraryProbability

end LatentDiffusion

28structure ForceRegularity (F : H → H) (m : ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0) : Prop where29  monotone : ∀ x y, m * ‖x - y‖ ^ 2 ≤ inner ℝ (F x - F y) (x - y)30  lipschitz : ∀ x y, ‖F x - F y‖ ≤ (L : ℝ) * ‖x - y‖
New theory

N2 — Stable step size

Mathematical statement

Require

λ>0,h>0,λh≤1,hL2≤λ.\lambda>0,\qquad h>0,\qquad\lambda h\le1,\qquad hL^2\le\lambda.λ>0,h>0,λh≤1,hL2≤λ.

For L>0L>0L>0, the familiar sufficient condition is 0<h≤min⁡{1/λ,λ/L2}0<h\le\min\{1/\lambda,\lambda/L^2\}0<h≤min{1/λ,λ/L2}. These restrictions depend on the complete force constants.

/-!
# Quantitative stability and discretization error for latent Euler algorithms

These results concern actual Euler updates on a real inner product space.  In the
paper's interacting algorithm that space can be the latent parameter / particle
cloud with its particle-normalized inner product.  Neither contraction nor an
error recurrence is included among the hypotheses.

The reference-path consistency hypothesis below is a *local defect bound*.  An
SDE application must establish it from the drift and Brownian regularity; this
file does not claim that such a bound follows from monotonicity alone.
-/

open scoped NNReal

namespace LatentDiffusion

variable {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]

/-- Added regularity assumption on the positive force, i.e. minus the SDE drift.
The constant `L` is nonnegative by its type. -/

/-- A step restriction stated without division, including degenerate spaces. -/

/-- The Euler update, with the entire additive noise increment supplied as `ξ`.
For IPLD it is `sqrt (2h)` times the appropriately scaled Gaussian cloud. -/

/-- The actual numerical trajectory, rather than an assumed error recurrence. -/

/-- Shared additive noise cancels, and strong monotonicity yields the sharp
quadratic one-step coefficient. -/

/-- A simpler squared contraction with a transparent step restriction. -/

/-- Norm contraction sufficient for robust coupling and numerical consistency. -/

/-- The familiar minimum step restriction implies the division-free one. -/

/-- A single update separates force approximation error from the reference's
local discretization defect. No stochastic independence is required. -/

/-- Finite-horizon robust numerical bound, including the exact geometric factor.
`G` is the implemented force; `F` is the reference force. The reference can be an
exact SDE skeleton once the stated local defect estimate has been established. -/

/-- Uniform numerical and model bias: `2 B / m + (2 D / m) sqrt h`.
The dimension and number of particles do not enter this algebraic estimate. -/

end LatentDiffusion

namespace LatentDiffusion

variable {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]

/-- Squared coupling error averaged over a finite probability space. -/

/-- Explicit finite probability weights. Normalization gives the expression its
usual expectation interpretation; the algebraic estimates only need positivity. -/

/-- Euler with a shared additive increment and an additional stochastic force
innovation `ζ`, multiplied by the step size. -/

/-- The zero cross moment needed from a centered innovation is stated on the
current Euler displacement. Conditional mean zero given the current states and
shared increment is a sufficient probabilistic condition for this assumption. -/

/-- Pythagorean identity after averaging: only the explicit cross moment is used. -/

/-- Centered stochastic force error has a mean-square floor of order `h`, rather
than the order-one floor for an arbitrary bounded force error. The result is for
actual coupled Euler recursions on any finite probability space. -/

end LatentDiffusion

namespace LatentDiffusion

open MeasureTheory

variable {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H]

/-- Primitive assumptions on exact integral reference segments. In an `L²`
realization `G` bounds the drift root mean square and `N sqrt t` bounds the
Brownian-increment root mean square. These are moment assumptions, not a local
numerical error or contraction assumption. `W` is the additive noise path. -/

/-- The local consistency bound is derived from the exact integral equation,
the drift moment bound, and the square-root noise increment bound. -/

/-- Nonasymptotic Euler error derived from primitive integral-path moment bounds,
with separate numerical bias `O(h G + N sqrt h)` and force-model bias `O(B)`.
The ambient space can be an `L²` Hilbert space, in which case this is an RMS
coupling estimate. An SDE existence theorem and verification of its stated
moment and lifted-force assumptions are separate obligations. -/

end LatentDiffusion

N6 — Frozen reference and empirical-force residual

Mathematical statement

In the genuine space L2(Ω;scaled cloud)L^2(\Omega;\text{scaled cloud})L2(Ω;scaled cloud), a reference force RRR is LLL-Lipschitz and admits actual segments satisfying N4, with nonnegative drift radius GGG and noise bound WtW\sqrt tWt​. It need not contract in the fixed parameter coordinate.

The actual physical parameter projection CCC has norm at most one and satisfies Cyn=a⋆Cy_n=a_\starCyn​=a⋆​ almost surely for every nnn. The norms in N4 are root mean squares. The construction and stationarity of a frozen posterior process, and its uniform drift/noise moment bounds, must be supplied by the application. The theorem accepts any such fixed reference parameter. An inference guarantee to the paper's tilted maximizer additionally identifies this a⋆a_\stara⋆​ with the optimizer proved in Part I.

Theorem New 1 — Uniform inference error with a stochastic oracle

Mathematical statement

Let K=MN>0K=MN>0K=MN>0, and impose A3–A4 on each actual datum potential and N2, N5–N7 on the reference and innovations. Construct the complete interacting force FKF_KFK​ from those potentials, and use its actual noisy Euler update Xn+1=Xn−hFK(Xn)+ξn+hζnX_{n+1}=X_n-hF_K(X_n)+\xi_n+h\zeta_nXn+1​=Xn​−hFK​(Xn​)+ξn​+hζn​. Write an=CXna_n=CX_nan​=CXn​ for the physical parameter and q=1−λh/2q=1-\lambda h/2q=1−λh/2. For every n≥0n\ge0n≥0,

(E∥an−a⋆∥2)1/2≤qn∥X0−y0∥L2+2λVK+Lλ(hG+43Wh)+hσ2λ.\begin{aligned}\left(\mathbb E\|a_n-a_\star\|^2\right)^{1/2}\le{}&q^n\|X_0-y_0\|_{L^2}+\frac2\lambda\sqrt{\frac VK}\\&+\frac L\lambda\left(hG+\frac43W\sqrt h\right)+\sqrt{\frac{h\sigma^2}{\lambda}}.\end{aligned}(E∥an​−a⋆​∥2)1/2≤​qn∥X0​−y0​∥L2​+λ2​KV​​+λL​(hG+34​Wh​)+λhσ2​​.​

The force regularity is derived from the original per-datum potentials, including the exact pointwise-to-L2L^2L2 lift. The output norm is proved equal to the physical parameter root mean-square error. The four explicit terms quantify initialization, finite-particle averaging, temporal discretization and the centered stochastic oracle. The finite-population identity below calibrates oracle variance from batch dispersion.

The bound is uniform in the number of steps. Its target a⋆a_\stara⋆​ is the fixed reference parameter specified in N6; interpreting it as convergence to the paper's optimizer requires that identification and a corresponding frozen posterior reference. It retains explicit reference existence, moment and innovation premises; it does not claim convergence of the unrestricted Adam/preconditioned implementation.

What this adds to the paper. The paper gives an implicit full-batch error rate. This bound shows how much error comes from initialization, a finite particle cloud, finite time steps and a noisy gradient oracle, under the stated reference assumptions.

Theorem New 2 — Two explicit minibatch temperature corrections

Mathematical statement

Random scan: select both an uninflated drift and its 2h\sqrt{2h}2h​ noise with probability ppp, leaving the particle fixed otherwise. Its scalar second-moment fixed point is

vscan=1a(1−ah/2).v_{\mathrm{scan}}=\frac1{a(1-ah/2)}.vscan​=a(1−ah/2)1​.

Full noise: retain the inverse-inclusion drift and replace the printed noise by 2h W\sqrt{2h}\,W2h​W on every particle. Its second-moment fixed point is

vfull=1a(1−ah/(2p)).v_{\mathrm{full}}=\frac1{a(1-ah/(2p))}.vfull​=a(1−ah/(2p))1​.

The denominators must be nonzero in the algebraic identities. For meaningful positive stable scalar moments take a>0a>0a>0 and respectively 0<ah<20<ah<20<ah<2 or 0<ah<2p0<ah<2p0<ah<2p. These exact quadratic calculations expose the remaining Euler bias and the 1/p1/p1/p cost of random drift. They do not assert invariant-law existence for the adaptive nonlinear algorithm.

What this adds to the paper. These two scalar repairs restore the intended small-step temperature. They show that changing the batch size can change the target unless drift and noise are scaled consistently.

/-!
# Exact mini-batch noise and temperature audit

For one fixed datum, a uniform batch of size B among M data has inclusion
probability p = B/M. Algorithm 1 uses an inverse-inclusion drift h/p when the
datum is selected, but adds Gaussian noise of variance 2hp to every particle.
The calculations below integrate the actual standard Gaussian; no diffusion
limit or invariant-law assumption is used. In particular, the source's claimed
variance matching fails even for the one-dimensional quadratic potential.

The scalar moment chains are defined recursions, derived from the exact
one-step conditional Gaussian moment. They do not assert existence or
convergence of a nonlinear adaptive Adam sampler.
-/

namespace LatentDiffusion.BatchAudit

/-- Inverse-inclusion scaling gives the full drift in expectation. -/

/-- Actual Gaussian conditional second moment, with specified noise variance. -/

/-- The Gaussian integration is proved from its first two moments. -/

/-- The paper noises every particle with variance `2hp`, even if unselected. -/

/-- Exact moment of Algorithm 1 for the quadratic potential `a x²/2`. -/
